687.name: redirect
687.docs:
Redirect Handling

By default, a `Client` will automatically handle HTTP redirects, having a
maximum redirect chain of 10 hops. To customize this behavior, a
`redirect::Policy` can be used with a `ClientBuilder`.

246.name: Policy
246.docs:
A type that controls the policy on how to handle the following of redirects.

The default value will catch redirect loops, and has a maximum of 10
redirects it will follow in a chain before returning an error.

610.name: limited
610.docs:
Create a `Policy` with a maximum number of redirects.

An `Error` will be returned if the max is reached.

611.name: none
611.docs: Create a `Policy` that does not follow any redirect.

612.name: custom
612.docs:
Create a custom `Policy` using the passed function.

# Note

615.name: redirect

A type that holds information on the next request and previous requests

644.docs: Returns an action meaning reqwest should follow the next URL.

645.docs:
Returns an action meaning reqwest should not follow the next URL.

733.name: retry
733.docs:
Retry requests

A `Client` has the ability to retry requests, by sending additional copies
to the server if a response is considered retryable.

249.name: Builder
249.docs:
Builder to configure retries

Construct with [`for_host()`].

705.name: scoped
705.docs:
Create a scoped retry policy.

For a more convenient constructor, see [`for_host()`].

706.name: no_budget
706.docs:
Set no retry budget.

Sets that no budget will be enforced. This could also be considered
to be an infinite budget.

707.name: max_extra_load
707.docs:
Sets the max extra load the budget will allow.

Think of the amount of requests your client generates, and how much
load that puts on the server. This option configures as a percentage
how much extra load is allowed via retries.

708.name: max_retries_per_request
708.docs:
Set the max retries allowed per request.

For each logical (initial) request, only retry up to `max` times.

709.name: classify_fn
709.docs:
Provide a classifier to determine if a request should be retried.

# Example

710.name: classify
710.docs: Provide a classifier to determine if a request should be retried.

704.name: for_host
704.docs:
Create a retry builder with a request scope.

To provide a scope that isn't a closure, use the more general
[`Builder::scoped()`].

732.name: never
732.docs:
Create a retry policy that will never retry any request.

This is useful for disabling the `Client`s default behavior of retrying
protocol nacks.

2.name: Error

The Errors that may occur when processing a `Request`.

Note: Errors may include the full URL used to make the `Request`. If the URL
contains sensitive information (e.g. an API key as a query parameter), be
sure to remove it ([`without_url`](Error::without_url))

entirely.

241.name: no_gzip
241.docs:
Disable auto response body gzip decompression.

This method exists even if the optional `gzip` feature is not enabled.
This can be used to ensure a `Client` doesn't use gzip decompression
even if another dependency were to enable the optional `gzip` feature.

242.name: no_brotli
242.docs:
Disable auto response body brotli decompression.

This method exists even if the optional `brotli` feature is not enabled.
This can be used to ensure a `Client` doesn't use brotli decompression
even if another dependency were to enable the optional `brotli` feature.

243.name: no_zstd
243.docs:
Disable auto response body zstd decompression.

This method exists even if the optional `zstd` feature is not enabled.
This can be used to ensure a `Client` doesn't use zstd decompression
even if another dependency were to enable the optional `zstd` feature.

244.name: no_deflate
244.docs:
Disable auto response body deflate decompression.

This method exists even if the optional `deflate` feature is not enabled.
This can be used to ensure a `Client` doesn't use deflate decompression
even if another dependency were to enable the optional `deflate` feature.

254.name: timeout
254.docs:
Enables a total request timeout.

The timeout is applied from when the request starts connecting until the
response body has finished. Also considered a total deadline.

256.name: read_timeout
256.docs:
Enables a read timeout.

The timeout applies to each read operation, and resets after a
successful read. This is more appropriate for detecting stalled
connections when the size isn't known beforehand.

257.name: connect_timeout
257.docs:
Set a timeout for only the connect phase of a `Client`.

Default is `None`.

258.name: connection_verbose
258.docs:
Set whether connections should emit verbose logs.

Enabling this option will emit [log][] messages at the `TRACE` level
for read and write operations on connections.

166.name: pool_idle_timeout
166.docs:
Set an optional timeout for idle sockets being kept-alive.

Pass `None` to disable timeout.

167.name: pool_max_idle_per_host
167.docs:
Sets the maximum idle connection per host allowed in the pool.

Default is `usize::MAX` (no limit).

259.name: http1_title_case_headers

Set whether HTTP/1 connections will accept spaces between header
names and the colon that follow them in responses.

Newline codepoints (`\r` and `\n`) will be transformed to spaces when
parsing.

Restrict the Client to be used with HTTPS only requests.

275.name: no_hickory_dns
275.docs:
Disables the hickory-dns async resolver.

This method exists even if the optional `hickory-dns` feature is not enabled.
This can be used to ensure a `Client` doesn't use the hickory-dns async resolver
even if another dependency were to enable the optional `hickory-dns` feature.

276.name: resolve
276.docs:
Override DNS resolution for specific domains to a particular IP address.

Set the port to `0` to use the conventional port for the given scheme (e.g. 80 for http).
Ports in the URL itself will always be used instead of the port in the overridden addr.

278.name: resolve_to_addrs

Override DNS resolution for specific domains to particular IP addresses.

Set the port to `0` to use the conventional port for the given scheme (e.g. 80 for http).
Ports in the URL itself will always be used instead of the port in the overridden addr.

still be applied on top of this resolver.

Overrides for specific names passed to `resolve` and `resolve_to_addrs` will
still be applied on top of this resolver.

370.name: query
370.docs:
Modify the query string of the URL.

Modifies the URL of this request, adding the parameters provided.
This method appends and does not overwrite. This means that it can
be called multiple times and that existing query parameters are not
overwritten if the same key is used. The key will simply show up
twice in the query string.
Calling `.query(&[("foo", "a"), ("foo", "b")])` gives `"foo=a&foo=b"`.

580.docs:
Returns a new no-proxy configuration based on environment variables (or `None` if no variables are set)

579.name: from_string
579.docs:
Returns a new no-proxy configuration based on a `no_proxy` string (or `None` if no variables
are set)
The rules are as follows:
* The environment variable `NO_PROXY` is checked, if it is not set, `no_proxy` is checked
* If neither environment variable is set, `None` is returned
* Entries are expected to be comma-separated (whitespace between entries is ignored)
* IP addresses (both IPv4 and IPv6) are allowed, as are optional subnet masks (by adding /size,
  for example "`192.168.1.0/24`").
* An entry "`*`" matches all hostnames (this is the only wildcard allowed)
* Any other entry is considere
